findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: SECOND REPEAT: Inspector observed jalapeños (stated to have been opened yesterday by the person in charge (PIC)) being stored in the can. CORRECTED- kitchen staff transferred the contents of the can into a food safe container. The original can is not rated to safely hold the food material after opening the can. Ensure acidic food items from cans (such as jalapeños and tomato paste) are transferred (and date marked) into a food safe container if held over 24 hours to prevent contamination of ready to eat foods.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed raw chicken and beef stored above ready to eat items (tamales and cut vegetables) in the walk in cooler. CORRECTED-kitchen staff moved the chicken to the bottom shelf, and the beef between the chicken and ready to eat foods. Ensure that food items are stored in a manner that protects against cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed cut lettuce in an open container below the refrigeration lines in the walk in cooler. CORRECTED- a lid was placed over the lettuce. Ensure all foods in cooling units are covered to protect against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an accumulation of soil debris at the soda gun nozzle at the bar. CORRECTED- the item was cleaned and sanitized. Ensure all food contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed foods in the toppings prep cooler to have internal temperatures between 45-48F. CORRECTED foods were voluntarily discarded. Replacement items were put in an ice bath. All items in the top of the cooler are time/ temperature control for food safety (TCS); (pico de gallo, cut tomatoes, shredded lettuce, shredded cheese, and sour cream). TCS foods must be keep below 41F, above 135F, or moved under time as control (to be used or discarded within 4 hours). Discussed monitoring foods on ice bath with a thermometer, or using small batches and implementing time as control.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the toppings prep cooler failing to hold TCS foods at or below 41F- see violation #22. A follow up inspection is scheduled for 7/17 to verify compliance. Ensure the unit has been serviced or replaced by this date. All cold holding units must have the capacity to hold TCS foods at or below 41F.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed the gaskets on the bottom of the protein prep cooler to be separating. Replace gaskets by the next routine inspection to ensure equipment is in proper repair.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the kitchen hand washing sink to have separated from the wall. Reset the screws into the wall and re-caulk sink to the wall to prevent the entry and harborage of mold.

findings.comment: Inspector observed pork stored below chicken in the walk in cooler. CORRECTED-kitchen staff moved the chicken below the pork to reflect correct storage order. Due to the fact that chicken (165F) requires a higher internal cooking temperature than pork (145F), it must be stored below the raw pork. Ensure that food items are stored in a manner that protects against cross-contamination.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an open container of cranberry juice labeled “Refrigerate after opening” sitting at room temperature (internal temperature of 63F) at the bar. CORRECTED- the PIC confirmed the container had not been open for more than 3 hours. The bottle was immediately moved into cold holding. Temperature control for food safety items (TCS) (including those labeled “Refrigerate after opening “ or “Keep refrigerated”) must be cold held at or below 41F, and date marked like all other TCS food items. Read labels of hermetically sealed containers regarding safe storage after opening to prevent temperature abuse and potential food-borne illness.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple TCS foods to be out of the seven day range of date marking:
1) Tamales dated 2/23
2) Cream cheese dated 2/26
3) Salsa dated 3/2 and 3/10
CORRECTED- the tamales and cream cheese were voluntarily discarded. The salsa had the incorrect dates, and was confirmed to have been prepared on 3/13. New dates were applied to reflect the date of preparation. Ensure date stickers are removed during ware washing and items are marked with the date of preparation (day one), to be used or discarded within seven days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: No Certified Food Protection Manager (CFM/ CFPM) was on site at the start of today’s inspection. CORRECTED- CFM arrived about 15 minutes into the inspection. A CFM must be present at all times food is being prepared or served. Inspector provided the PIC a list of ANAB-accredited Certified Food Protection Manager Courses, which includes tests that are available in Spanish. Ensure a CFM is always present during the facility’s hours of operation to oversee proper food handling and temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.comment: Inspector observed partially cooked chicken nuggets stored below raw scallops and shrimp in the double door freezer in the facility’s back room. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) directed staff to move chicken nuggets to the top. Ensure any partially cooked animal proteins are stored above raw animal proteins to prevent contamination of food. Ready to eat foods should be stored at the top of a cooling unit, followed by animals proteins that require increasing cooking temperatures- with the protein requiring the highest cooking temperature at the bottom.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the dish washing machine to not be dispensing a chemical sanitizer (0 ppm Cl). CORRECTED- PIC called their service provider to obtain more sanitizer. The sanitizer was replaced and observed to be properly dispensing sanitizer (100 ppm Cl). Ensure frequent testing of sanitizer solution using the facility’s test strips. Dish machines that sanitize chemically should be dispense 50-200 ppm Cl bleach to properly sanitizer food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple time/temperature control for food safety (TCS) items to be without date marking. Items included, but are not limited to, cheese sauce, salsa verde, salsa, onion, cilantro, cheese, and tamales. CORRECTED- PIC marked each item with the day they were prepared or thawed. Ensure all TCS foods being held at the facility for over 24 hours are date marked.

findings.comment: Inspector observed light entering the facility along the left side of the back door. Ensure all outer openings are protected from the entry of pests. Apply new weather stripping by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. [C]

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed cups lacking handles being stored in the sugar tub underneath the chip area prep table. CORRECTED- The person in charge removed cups from food storage container. Discussed proper utensil storage for in-use utensils with the person in charge. Ensure the usage of scoops with HANDLES sticking outwards to prevent contamination of food.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container. [C]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Inspector observed one Food Handler Certificate to have been expired since September, and two wait staff to not have their Food Handler’s Certificates. Ensure all employees handling food or ice obtain their Food Handler’s Certificates within 30 days of hire. Food Handlers must renew their certificate every three years to ensure safe food handling practices.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
It has been observed that the facility’s CFM has allowed their Allergen training to expire. Ensure all CFMs have their Allergen Awareness Training, and renew this certificate every three years. Inspector provided literature regarding Allergen Awareness requirements, which includes a link to ANSI-approved Allergen awareness training programs.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed staff to turn off the faucet with their bare hands after washing hands. CORRECTED- Education occurred regarding hand washing procedures. Inspector provided a hand washing infographic in both English and Spanish to the facility. Ensure a clean barrier is used after washing hands to turn off the faucet to prevent recontaminating hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

CORRECTED- hand washing sinks will be the only place where staff wash hands. Hand washing signs were provided to the operator.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
The following raw animal proteins were observed to be stored in a manner that does not protect against contamination:
- Raw chicken was observed stored above beef in the walk in cooler
- Raw shelled eggs were stored above ready-to-eat foods such as but not limited to avocados, lemons, and limes

The raw animal proteins were rearranged during the inspection and the violations were corrected on site. Discussed proper storage order with PIC.  Foods that have higher cooking temperatures should always be stored below items with a lesser cooking temperature. Ensure that food items are stored in a manner that protects against cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Several containers of cooked foods were observed without date marking. These items in the walk in cooler include but aren't limited to chicken, beans, and beef. Discussed proper date marking with PIC. Ensure that any TCS food items that are stored in house longer than 24 hours are date marked and discarded if not used within 7 days of preparation.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: There were several ants observed along the wall of the service station. Discussed and shown to the PIC. The PIC noted that Orkin services the facility and that a follow-up will occur in two weeks to monitor the presence of insects. The facility was instructed to have Orkin provide treatment more frequently (at least 1x a week). Be sure to routinely clean the establishment to help reduce the presence of insects.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
1) In the veg prep cooler, an employee’s raw shell eggs were observed stored on the top shelf, above sour cream and salsas. CORRECTED- The eggs were moved to storage in the right side of the 2 door cooler, which is used for personal items. 
2) In the walk-in cooler, raw meats were observed stored above lemons and cooked meats. Raw chicken was observed stored above raw beef. CORRECTED- Reviewed proper storage order with PIC, who rearranged storage. Storage order signage is posted near the walk-in cooler door. Review this information with food employees.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. [P]

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Foods in the steam table were observed at or below 120F (probed). Refried beans were observed at 120F, rice at 100F, ground beef at 110F, chicken at 120F, and sauce at 119F. CORRECTED- All foods had been properly cooked or reheated prior to being placed in the steam table. Foods were rapidly reheated in the oven or on the stovetop to 165F, then returned to the steam table. Monitor hot holding temperatures to ensure that the steam table is holding foods at 135F or above.
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above. [P]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
3rd REPEAT: Back door is not tight fitting. Daylight is still visible around the bottom and left edges of the door. Trim has been added to eliminate gaps outside of the door opening. PIC has further plans to eliminate gaps around the back door.
6-202.15: (A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents. (B) Does not apply to FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS which opens into larger structure. (C) Exterior doors need not be self-closing if designed for limited-use. (D) If opening present, opening shall be protected against rodent and insects. (E) Paragraph (D) not applicable when pests are absent. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
The gasket on the right door of the protein prep cooler is separated from the door in several places. Replace the gasket so it’s properly attached and seals the door shut.
4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation. [C]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: There was no sanitizer bucket prepared upon inspector’s arrival. CORRECTED- A sanitizer bucket was made upon request. Sanitizer buckets must be prepared and available during all times of food prep and service.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11 (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. [C]

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: A signed employee reporting agreement was not available for one of the two food employees present during this inspection. CORRECTED- PIC Reviewed the agreement with the employee, who then signed the reporting agreement. Review the employee health policy with employees before they work their first shift. Keep signed reporting agreements on file for review during health inspections.
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  [Pf]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
A food employee was observed washing a shaker in the kitchen handsink, then drying the shaker with a towel. CORRECTED- Inspector discussed with PIC that handsinks are only to be used for handwashing. PIC will discuss with employees.
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The dish machine was observed with 10ppm Cl in the rinse after two cycles. CORRECTED- PIC changed the sanitizer concentrate bucket and primed the machine. Sanitizer was then observed at 100ppm. Use test strips to monitor the dish machine’s sanitizer rinse concentration.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have a concentration of 50-200ppm. [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Five to eight small containers of salsa were observed on the wait station counter with internal temperatures of 73F. PIC stated that salsa is held on the counter during lunch, then returned to the cooler. CORRECTED- Inspector discussed using Time as a Control, and a policy was created. Salsas will be held on the counter during a service period of no more than 4 hours. Any remaining at the end of 4 hours will be discarded. Out of temperature salsas were removed from cold holding at open (11am) and will be used or discarded by 3pm.
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Milk and tamales in the 2 door cooler, a container of cream cheese in the veggie prep cooler, and a container of cooked chicken in the walk-in cooler were observed without date-markings. CORRECTED- PIC stated that foods were prepared either today (milk) or yesterday (tamales, chicken, cream cheese) and labeled them accordingly. Ensure all TCS foods are labeled with the date they were opened or prepared. Foods may be discarded if they are found without date-markings in the future.
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1. [Pf]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
2nd REPEAT: Back door is not tight fitting. Daylight is still visible around the edges (specifically on the left edge of the door) and in some places, around the edge of the door frame itself. Repair door and frame so that it’s sealed against pests.
6-202.15: (A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents. (B) Does not apply to FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS which opens into larger structure. (C) Exterior doors need not be self-closing if designed for limited-use. (D) If opening present, opening shall be protected against rodent and insects. (E) Paragraph (D) not applicable when pests are absent. [C]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Fly strips were observed hanging above the dish machine drainboards and over a counter at the end of the cookline. Fly strips may be used over non-food surfaces or overnight, but must be taken down during the day when the facility is in operation. 
3-307.11: FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301-3-306. [C]

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
After washing a shaker in the cookline handsink, an employee was observed drying the shaker with a towel. CORRECTED- Discussed proper warewashing and air-drying procedures with PIC, who will review the practices with employees. Utensils must be washed, rinsed, sanitized, and air-dried.
4-901.11: After cleaning and SANITIZING, EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS: (A) shall be air dried or used after adequate draining before FOOD contact. (B) May not be cloth dried except that UTENSILS that have been air-dried may be polished with cloths that are clean and dry. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
2nd REPEAT: The following physical facilities areas still in need of attention:
1) Seal floor/step at the entrance of the walk-in cooler.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Employee foods (milk, cereal, condiments, pasta salad, etc) were observed intermixed with foods for service in the 2 door cooler, the walk-in cooler, the freezers, and on the shelves of the wait station. Designate areas for the storage of personal items below or completely separate from the areas used for foods for service. Keep employee items separate from those used for the operation of the restaurant.
6-501.110: (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions. [C]

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
There was no CFM present upon inspector’s arrival. Additionally, multiple Priority and Priority Foundation violations were observed. Review employee health policies, handwashing, handsink use, and cooling processes with employees. Inspector will follow up to see signed reporting agreements and review these items further.
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16. [Pf]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
A CFM was not present when the inspector arrived. CORRECTED- PIC (a CFM) arrived before the end of the inspection. Ensure sufficient CFMs are on staff and scheduled to cover all shifts of food prep and service. The facility must always be under the supervision of an on-site certified food protection manager.
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
Signed employee reporting agreements were not available for the employees present during this inspection. Review the employee health policy with employees before they work their first shift. Keep signed reporting agreements on file for review during health inspections. Inspector provided a blank reporting agreement in both English and Spanish. Make copies, review with staff, and keep the signed copies on file.
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  [Pf]

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
Facility does not have a vomit/diarrhea clean up policy available. Inspector provided a clean up policy in both English and Spanish. Keep this policy for reference in case vomit/diarrhea clean up is needed.
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. [Pf]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
A food employee was observed entering the kitchen and immediately handling clean dishes without washing hands. A food employee was also observed moving from handling dirty dishes to clean without washing hands. Review when to wash hands with all food employees. Ensure employees wash their hands upon entering the kitchen, when changing tasks, and after handling dirty dishes.
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  [P]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
The bar handsink basin contained limes, ice, and straws when inspector arrived. CORRECTED- An employee cleaned out the sink. Handsinks must ONLY be used for handwashing and no other purpose.
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Pink slime accumulation was observed along the edge of the baffle in the ice machine. Clean the baffle as often as needed to prevent soil accumulation.
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment:
Three buckets and one pan of cheese sauce were not cooled from 135F to 70F within 2 hours. The cheese sauce was finished cooking at 11:30am. At 2:00pm, the cheese sauce temperatures were 74F in a pan near the grill and 96F, 101F, and 104F in buckets on the back prep counter. CORRECTED- Cheese sauce was voluntarily discarded. Monitor cooling foods and use cooling techniques to ensure they cool from 135F to 70F within 2 hours, and ultimately reach 41F within no more than 6 hours total.
3-501.14: (A) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within in 2 hours from 135F to 70F. Within 6 hours, FOOD shall cool from 135F to 41F or less. (B) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within 4 hours or less if prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature. (C) TCS FOOD received above 45F in compliance with LAWS shall be cooled within 4 hours. (D) Raw EGGS shall be received and immediately placed in EQUIPMENT with air temperature of 45F or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
A pan and three buckets of cheese sauce, a pan of cooked beef, and a pan of tamales were observed cooling on the back prep counter without additional cooling techniques in use. The cheese sauce was voluntarily discarded because it had not reached 70F within 2 hours. The beef was moved to the walk-in cooler. The tamales were 135F, and were spread out on a sheet tray and placed in the walk-in cooler to cool. Monitor cooling foods and use cooling methods to help foods cool quickly. 
3-501.15: (A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers shall be: arranged to maximize heat transfer through container walls, loosely covered or uncovered, and during cooling period. [C]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Back door is not tight fitting. Daylight is still visible around the edges (specifically on the left edge of the door) and in some places, around the edge of the door frame itself. Repair door and frame so that it’s sealed against pests.
6-202.15: (A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents. (B) Does not apply to FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS which opens into larger structure. (C) Exterior doors need not be self-closing if designed for limited-use. (D) If opening present, opening shall be protected against rodent and insects. (E) Paragraph (D) not applicable when pests are absent. [C]

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Four damp wiping cloths were observed sitting on coutertops and prep surfaces throughout the kitchen. Store wiping cloths submerged in sanitizer solution when not in use.
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. [C]

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
A knife was stored in the gap between the prep cooler and the steam table. CORRECTED- A food employee removed the knife to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Store in-use utensils on a clean surface, not between pieces of equipment.
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. [C]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: There was no sanitizer bucket prepared upon inspector’s arrival. CORRECTED- When PIC arrived, a sanitizer bucket was made upon request. Sanitizer buckets must be prepared and available during all times of food prep and service.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11 (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: The following physical facilities areas still in need of attention:
1) Finish the trim around the kitchen door to restrooms. There are gaps and the inside of the drywall material is exposed in some places.
2) Replace the broken floor tile in the kitchen between the two freezers.
3) Seal nudo panel to the wall behind the prep sink.
4) Seal floor/step at the entrance of the walk-in cooler.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]
